responses.review_design:1:1: fixed: §3.3 adds a row checked first: a non-null base not in the running engine's store is upstream 'unknown_base' (local 'unknown'), note 'recorded by a newer or unreleased plugin: upgrade the plugin to compare', no diff and no apply; null keeps the manual compare. §3.5: record.reviewed copies such bases unchanged and is omitted when every listed file is unknown_base. §9's unmerged-build risk degrades the same way. Test 11 covers skew: no downgrade offer, base kept, and no ping-pong when the newer engine reads the result.

output.summary: Revision 3 answers review_design:1:1: a non-null base that the running engine's history store lacks is reported as upstream unknown_base ('recorded by a newer or unreleased plugin: upgrade'), with no diff or apply, and record.reviewed keeps such bases unchanged (omitted when all listed files are in that state), so installs on different plugin versions cannot downgrade or ping-pong the record; test 11 covers it. It also takes the notes: the execute skill forbids editing TEMPLATE.json in a goal, prompts' copy/delete follow the workflow.json decision, and G1025 gets the same history-store note as G1022. The rest of the design (TEMPLATE.json record, content-addressed history store, non-blocking policy_update item in next/validate, read-only engine with a bootstrap-skill policy-branch update and decline) is unchanged.

findings.text: F1: an older plugin treats a newer recorded base as 'upstream changed', and its reviewed record downgrades the base. §3.3's last row lists a base that is null or not in the running engine's history store as upstream changed / local unknown, with a manual compare against the running template; record.reviewed resets every base to the running S. Plugin version skew is normal here (two marketplace caches, 6747a5e and c3791a0, plus the Codex engine on 15b59a5). An older plugin seeing B = S_new would offer its older template as 'the new default'. Writing its reviewed record sets B back to S_old, and the newer plugin then lists the file again: a ping-pong. Fix: a non-null base absent from the running store is reported as upstream: unknown_base ('recorded by a newer or unreleased plugin: upgrade to compare'), with no diff to the running template and no apply. record.reviewed keeps such bases unchanged, or is omitted when every listed file is in that state. null keeps the manual compare. Test: a record written with a larger store gives no downgrade direction, and its reviewed record leaves that base as it was.

2:1: installs on different plugin versions still ping-pong the record over files only one version ships. §3.5 drops record entries for files no longer shipped, and §3.3 lists 'B not in record, S present' as added/copy. After G1022 removes review_design.md, a post-G1022 plugin's reviewed record omits it. A pre-G1022 plugin then shows added/copy and writes it back, and the newer plugin shows removed/delete, round after round. Fix: reviewed keeps a tombstone for each file no longer shipped (e.g. a removed map holding the last base). An engine that still ships the file lists nothing when the tombstoned id is in its store or equals S, and treats it as unknown_base otherwise. An engine that no longer ships it lists nothing. Say how a reader that does not know the tombstone form behaves (invalid_record is acceptable). Extend test 11 with a removed file read alternately by both engines. Secondary: a base recorded by an unmerged build stays unknown_base on every engine, listed forever and impossible to decline; the skill should say to set it to null once the newest plugin still shows unknown_base.

output.summary: Changes requested (one new finding). review_design:1:1 is resolved for files both plugin versions ship: unknown_base has no diff or apply, reviewed keeps the base, and test 11 covers it. The three notes are taken (TEMPLATE.json goal-edit ban, workflow.json-first prompt decisions, G1025 history note). New 2:1: files that only one version ships still ping-pong, because reviewed drops entries for files no longer shipped and the older plugin re-adds them. Fix: keep tombstones in the record. Also, an unmerged-build base stays unknown_base forever; the skill should give a way to reset it to null. No owner question.

spec:
Found while dogfooding Release 1 (2026-11-01). Bootstrap copies the shipped templates (templates/default: POLICY.json, workflow.json, prompts/) into .zzzops/, and from then on nothing links the copy to its source. When a release changes the defaults, a repository is never told. This already happened here: G1016 changed the shipped test_design.md and implement.md wording, and this repo's .zzzops/prompts still has the old text. G1023's designer then tried to fix it in a goal diff, which integrate refuses (policy-paths). G1000 and G1022 will change the default graph itself, and every bootstrapped repository needs to hear about that.
The pre-reset engine had this: policy sections carried default provenance (accepted, changed, rejected) and a plugin upgrade produced a policy review. The reset dropped it.

Add it back in the reset's style, with no fallback at run time (policy stays fully explicit in the repository):
1. Bootstrap records which shipped default each policy file came from: an engine or template version plus a per-file digest of the template copy, in POLICY.json settings (or a small .zzzops/TEMPLATE.json, decided in the design).
2. `next` and `validate --policy` compare the repository's record with the shipped templates of the running engine. When a shipped default changed since bootstrap, they show a non-blocking `policy_update` item. It lists the files that changed upstream, whether the repository also changed each file locally (from the digest), and a diff command from the old default to the new one.
3. The item's next step is a reviewed policy change: open a `zzzops/policy/*` branch that applies the upstream changes and keeps local edits, and run `validate --policy-ref` for its impact. Add this to the bootstrap or execute skill. Declining records the decision, so the item does not recur until the defaults change again.
4. A repository with no record (bootstrapped before this goal) gets a one-time item saying the record is missing, with a command to create it from the current files.
5. Never change policy automatically, and never block goal work on this item.

Acceptance:
- Engine tests: an unchanged repo shows no item; a changed shipped prompt shows the item with the file and a working diff command; a locally edited file is marked as such; declining suppresses the item until the next change; a missing record gives the one-time item.
- The skill documents the policy-branch update and the decline.
- This repository's record is created through its next policy branch.
- This PR edits docs/design/SPEC.md and DESIGN.md for every contract change it makes (the sections in G1017's pending row), adds a HISTORY §4 row and deletes the G1024 pending row (G1017's rule).
title: Tell repositories when the shipped default policy changed, and offer a reviewed update
